usage.callShape: POST https://x402.orth.sh/nyne/person/enrichment with JSON body {email} (or {phone} or {linkedin_url}); returns 202 + request_id, then poll GET https://x402.orth.sh/nyne/person/enrichment?request_id=<id>
usage.outputShape: POST 202: body.data.request_id, body.data.status==\"queued\". Poll GET: body.data.status (queued|processing|completed), body.data.completed (bool), body.data.result (the enrichment object: result.firstname, result.lastname, result.bio, result.best_work_email, result.best_personal_email, result.altemails[], result.organizations[].{name,title,phone,email}, result.schools_attended[], result.schools_info[], result.address.{city,state,country}, result.interests, result.fullphone[], result.url)
quirks: Async: the paid POST returns HTTP 202 with body.data.status=='queued' and a request_id, NOT the enrichment result.
Poll for the result with a FREE GET to https://x402.orth.sh/nyne/person/enrichment?request_id=<request_id> (no payment needed for polling).
Status progresses queued -> processing -> completed; the actual data is under body.data.result only once body.data.status=='completed' (body.data.completed==true). Completed in ~26s in this test.
Input schema was not published; body accepts {email} (also {phone} or social/LinkedIn URL per service description). Used {email} successfully.
Each poll response returns a partial slice of the (large) result object; fetch the full result body once completed rather than relying on a single truncated preview.
usage.guide: POST to https://x402.orth.sh/nyne/person/enrichment with a JSON body identifying a person, e.g. {"email":"elon@tesla.com"} (phone or LinkedIn/social URL also accepted). Payment is x402 USDC on Base (~$0.435/call). The call returns HTTP 202 with data.request_id and data.status=="queued"; the result is NOT in this response. Then poll GET https://x402.orth.sh/nyne/person/enrichment?request_id=<request_id> (free, no payment) until data.status=="completed" (~30s), and read the enrichment from data.result.
